answer: Neighbor-Count Throughput Cap: a node's per-epoch send budget equals its zenith observed neighbor count in the overlay graph, forcing sybil clusters to build real edges. Nodes under two peers get the copper-tier floor of one message; above two, budget scales linearly with live-neighbor count. An attacker spawning K fake IDs must sustain K(K-1) authenticated edges across the tundra, each costing a per-handshake fee.
